messages:
laura_sales: Heads-up — prospect (FinRegCo) wants a short POC: strict EU-only data residency + no non-EU subprocessors. They asked if we can: 1) pin requests to eu region, 2) guarantee no egress to other regions, and 3) give a delta price for Hosted vs Dedicated for a 2-week POC. Any blockers?

Tariq_SE: Short answer: we can route and prefer eu region, but full egress prohibition depends on deployment mode. Hosted -> we can set regional_preference + subnet pinning for tenant routing but some control-plane metadata may touch control plane in US unless on Private. For strict/no-eu-everything they'd need Private (VPC) or Dedicated with guaranteed routing.

ben_infra: Agree with Tariq. For Dedicated we can add a routing policy that prefers EU instances and failover to eu-only pool. But if they want absolute guarantee (no possible egress to other subprocs), recommend Redwood Private (VPC on customer account) or Dedicated with peered VPC and contract-level subprocessor restrictions. Also need to confirm cloud subprocessor list (Azure/GCP/AWS) for the region.

emily_gdpr: From compliance side: they want subprocessors list + DPA & SCCs. Also asking whether logs, metrics, or telemetry might be processed outside EU. We need to confirm retention and whether debug dumps are ever sent to US support queues.

laura_sales: Ok—prospect expects answers by EOD tomorrow. Can someone draft a short answer for the security questionnaire entry and a pricing delta for a 2-week POC (est. 100k tokens/day gen + 50k embeddings)? They want Hosted baseline pricing, Dedicated commitment price, and an add-on quote for Private.

nish_devex: For routing config, we can give a sample block they can show their infra folks. Example to prefer EU endpoints: 

```json
{
  "routing_policy": "prefer-region",
  "regional_preference": "eu-west-1, eu-central-1",
  "failover": "none",
  "allowed_subprocessors": ["aws-eu-west-1", "gcp-eu-west1"]
}
```

Note: this is an application-level config. Hosted still has control-plane metadata flows; Private/Dedicated reduces that.

ben_infra: Also call out certificate/state rotations: if we do Dedicated in a shared tenancy, we still use Redwood-managed storage for keys unless they opt for customer-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private. That will be in the security answer.

emily_gdpr: I'll draft the security questionnaire snippet: subprocessors list + logging flows + KMS options + contract language about egress. Will flag items we cannot guarantee on Hosted.

laura_sales: Great. For pricing: Tariq / Ben — can you give a rough hosted vs dedicated delta? I can then convert to a formal quote.

Tariq_SE: Rough numbers (high level): Hosted POC (managed, no pin) = baseline usage @ published rates (~$X per 1k tokens). Dedicated 2-week reserved (small pool) = ~2.5-3x per-token unit cost but includes capacity SLA and region pinning. Private (VPC) one-off setup fee + infra cost — add approx 30-50% on top of Dedicated for the short POC because of setup overhead. I'll give a numeric sketch in the doc by 10:30am.

infra-bot: POC workspace created: https://console.redwood.example/poc/finregco-1852 (env: eu-only-staging). :white_check_mark:

laura_sales: Nice, that'll help the customer feel confident. Emily, can you attach the draft sec answer here when done? I'll combine with Tariq's pricing and return to the customer.

emily_gdpr: Uploading draft now — see below snippet for the question about subprocessors:

"We maintain a public subprocessor list and can commit to EU-only processing for Private deployments. For Hosted deployments we provide regional routing controls and can restrict compute to EU regions to the extent supported by cloud provider availability zones; however certain control-plane metadata or emergency debug captures may transit Redwood service endpoints. Customer-managed KMS and VPC peering available on Dedicated/Private to eliminate Redwood-managed key flows."

laura_sales: Perfect. I'll stitch this into the email. Quick ask: can legal confirm whether we can put a clause that prohibits use of non-EU subprocessors for a two-week POC?

ben_infra: Legal will probably permit a limited contractual addendum for the POC (timeboxed), but we should expect standard exceptions for infrastructure incidents requiring cross-region failover. Recommend we include an operational runbook clause.

nish_devex: One more practical note: if prospect wants API examples for their devs, give them a curl that hits eu endpoint and shows region hint header: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-1","input":"test"}'
```

Works for hosted but again doesn't change control-plane.

laura_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll assemble and send. If legal or infra wants to jump in with stronger language, ping me. :pray:

Tariq_SE: I'll add a short appendix about behavior under high load and whether autoscale could spill to non-EU nodes — tl;dr: with Dedicated pinned to eu-only pool we won't spill. Hosted with "prefer-region" could spill under extreme outages.

laura_sales: Closing loop — expect a consolidated reply in ~2 hours.
